title: Cloud Computing Concepts

header.html: Define cloud computing; Describe the shared responsibility model; Define cloud models, including public, private, and hybrid; Identify appropriate use cases for each cloud model; Describe the consumption-based model; Compare cloud pricing models; Describe serverless
the official AZ-900 study guide, skills measured as of July 20, 2026

toc.title: Cloud models: public, private and hybrid

html:
1What cloud computing is

Cloud computing is the delivery of computing services (servers, storage, databases, networking, software, analytics and more) over the internet, from a provider's datacenters, so you rent what you need instead of buying and running your own hardware.

Traditional datacenter Cloud
You buy servers up front You rent services on demand
You plan capacity for the peak You scale up and down as needed
You run the building, power and hardware The provider runs them
Capital spending Operating spending

Azure is Microsoft's cloud platform. It runs in Microsoft datacenters around the world.

2The shared responsibility model

In the cloud the provider and the customer share the work of security and operations. The split depends on the service type (Module 3).

Layer On-premises IaaS PaaS SaaS
Information and data You You You You
Devices (mobile and PC) You You You You
Accounts and identities You You You You
Identity and directory infrastructure You You Shared Shared
Applications You You Shared Provider
Network controls You You Shared Provider
Operating system You You Provider Provider
Physical hosts You Provider Provider Provider
Physical network You Provider Provider Provider
Physical datacenter You Provider Provider Provider

Exam tip

. Three things are always the customer's: your data, your devices and your accounts and identities. The physical datacenter, hosts and network are the provider's in every cloud model. The more managed the service (IaaS to PaaS to SaaS), the more the provider handles.

3Cloud models: public, private and hybrid

Model What it is Who owns the hardware Typical use
Public cloud Services built on resources owned and run by a provider and shared by many customers (called tenants) The provider Fast start, no hardware to buy, pay as you go
Private cloud Cloud resources used by one organization, in its own datacenter or hosted for it The organization (or a host for it) Strict control or rules that need dedicated hardware
Hybrid cloud A mix of public and private (on-premises) that work together Both Keep sensitive systems on-premises, use the cloud for growth

Identify the use case

Need in the question Model
No upfront hardware spending, quick deployment Public
Data must stay in a datacenter the organization controls, full control over hardware Private
Some systems must stay on-premises, but extra capacity is wanted in the cloud Hybrid
A legacy system cannot move, while new apps use the cloud Hybrid
An app needs to burst to the cloud for a short peak Hybrid
Exam tip

. Public cloud still keeps customers separate: shared hardware does not mean shared data. Azure Arc and Azure Stack products extend Azure services to on-premises and other places, which supports hybrid designs (Module 13).

4The consumption-based model

In the consumption-based model you pay only for what you use, with no upfront cost and no long-term commitment required.

  • No need to buy hardware in advance.
  • Pay per hour, per minute, per second, per operation or per GB, depending on the service.
  • Stop using the service and the charges stop.
  • Cost follows the actual use, so a short peak does not require paying for peak capacity all year.

5Cloud pricing models

This skill asks you to compare how cloud costs are shaped.

Model How you pay Good for
Capital expenditure (CapEx) Large upfront purchase of assets (servers, buildings) that you own and depreciate Traditional datacenters
Operational expenditure (OpEx) Pay as you go for services, billed as an ongoing expense Cloud, consumption-based
Pay-as-you-go Standard rates, no commitment, billed for use Unpredictable or short workloads
Reserved instances / savings plans Beyond the study guide Commit to one or three years for a lower rate Steady, predictable workloads
Exam tip

. CapEx is the old on-premises style (you buy), OpEx is the cloud style (you rent). The cloud shifts spending from CapEx to OpEx.

6Serverless

Serverless computing lets you run code or services without managing servers. The servers still exist, but the provider manages them, scales them automatically and bills only while your code runs.

  • You focus on code or logic, not on virtual machines or operating systems.
  • Scaling is automatic, including down to zero use.
  • Examples on Azure: Azure Functions (run code in response to events) and Azure Logic Apps (workflows). Beyond the study guide for Logic Apps.
Serverless means Serverless does not mean
No servers for you to manage No servers exist
Pay for execution Always free
Automatic scale Fixed capacity

7Exam Q&A

7.1 Practice questions (choose the best answer)

S1Fabrikam Outdoors must keep customer records in a datacenter it fully controls, but wants to use Azure for a new web shop. Which cloud model fits?

  • APublic cloud only
  • BPrivate cloud only
  • CServerless
  • DHybrid cloud
Show the answer

Answer: D. Hybrid combines on-premises or private systems with public cloud services. Public only would move the records out; private only would not give the cloud benefits for the shop; serverless is a compute style, not a cloud model.

S2Which responsibility always belongs to the customer, whatever the service type?

  • AThe physical datacenter
  • BThe physical network
  • CThe hypervisor on the physical hosts
  • DThe data and the accounts that access it
Show the answer

Answer: D. Information and data, devices, and accounts and identities are always the customer's. The physical datacenter, hosts and network belong to the provider.

S3A company wants to stop buying servers and pay monthly only for the capacity it uses. Which spending shift describes this?

  • AFrom OpEx to CapEx
  • BFrom CapEx to OpEx
  • CFrom public to private
  • DFrom hybrid to on-premises
Show the answer

Answer: B. The cloud replaces large upfront capital purchases with ongoing operating expenses based on consumption.

S4A team wants to run a small piece of code whenever a file arrives, with no virtual machines to manage and billing only while the code runs. Which approach is this?

  • AServerless computing
  • BPrivate cloud
  • CCapital expenditure
  • DA dedicated physical server
Show the answer

Answer: A. Serverless runs code on demand, scales automatically and bills for execution, without server management by the customer.

S5Which statement about the public cloud is true?

  • AOnly one organization uses the hardware, and the customer owns it
  • BThe customer must buy the physical servers before using any service
  • CIt cannot be combined with on-premises systems in a hybrid design
  • DHardware is shared by many customers, but each customer's data stays separate
Show the answer

Answer: D. The provider owns the hardware and many tenants share it, with their data isolated. Public cloud can be part of a hybrid design.

S6Under the consumption-based model, what happens when you stop using a service?

  • AThe usage charges stop
  • BYou still pay the full monthly price
  • CYou pay a penalty
  • DThe hardware is shipped to you
Show the answer

Answer: A. You pay for what you use, so when use stops the usage charges stop. Some resources may still cost money while they exist, such as a stopped-but-allocated resource, so check the service.

7.2 Recall questions

R1Define cloud computing in one sentence.

Show the answer

Delivery of computing services over the internet from a provider's datacenters, so you rent what you need.

R2Which three things are always the customer's responsibility?

Show the answer

Data, devices, and accounts and identities.

R3Which cloud model is used by one organization only?

Show the answer

Private cloud.

R4Which model combines public cloud with on-premises systems?

Show the answer

Hybrid cloud.

R5CapEx or OpEx: which one is pay as you go?

Show the answer

OpEx (operational expenditure).

R6What does serverless mean?

Show the answer

You run code without managing servers; the provider scales and bills only for execution.

R7In which model does the provider manage the operating system, but not your applications?

Show the answer

PaaS (Module 3).

8Quick Reference Card

Topic Key fact
Cloud computing services over the internet, rented on demand
Shared responsibility customer always owns data, devices, accounts; provider always owns the physical datacenter, hosts and network; the rest shifts with IaaS, PaaS, SaaS
Public provider-owned, shared hardware, pay as you go
Private one organization, own or dedicated hardware
Hybrid public plus private or on-premises together
Consumption-based pay only for what you use; no upfront cost
CapEx vs OpEx CapEx = buy upfront; OpEx = pay as you go (cloud)
Serverless no server management, automatic scale, pay per execution (Azure Functions)
